X.note: Matted archival print on a dark vignette, with a clean name card that has an accent bar. It identifies the person, office and date at once. The bottom gradient washes over the lower part of the print and the card sits slightly off-balance. Credit text is small but legible.

Y.note: Full-bleed street photo that is atmospheric but low-contrast and hazy. The caption 'judges deferred to local lawmakers' has no visible link to a leafy street and a mansion, and nothing says where or when the street is. The long credit line is tiny and low-contrast, with a dark gradient strip behind it that is only partly effective. White text sits over the bright, hazy sky-to-ground transition.

why: X names its subject, office and date in large, high-contrast text next to a framed photo, while Y's generic caption and tiny credit leave the image's meaning and place unclear.
top_fix_for_weaker: Add a specific place/date label (e.g. 'Detroit street, c. 1900') tied to the claim, make the caption larger on a stronger dark scrim, and enlarge and shorten the source credit so it reads on a phone.
